messages:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing repeated latency SLO misses on the generation path in both us-west-2 and eu-west-2 for the past ~45m. Graph looks like a sawtooth: queues fill, max_batch triggers, then a drop, repeat.
rajesh: Yep, same. Continuous stream of small requests -> packer keeps hitting max_batch and admission stalls. Tail goes >500ms.
oliver: incident-bot posted alerts: `latency.p95 > 350ms` on /v1/generate in the dedicated pools.
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency.p95 breach on route /v1/generate — affected clusters: rwd-dedicated-usw2-01, rwd-dedicated-euw2-02 :rotating_light:
anna: Quick trio of observations: 1) request size skewed toward tiny prompts (20-50 tokens) 2) prefill KV cache miss rate up ~3x after the morning deploy 3) admission controller log shows lots of immediate max_batch hits so no batching headroom.
maria: Sharing a small excerpt from the admission controller logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-18T09:12:10Z admission: enqueued=132 max_batch=128 dispatched=0 reason=max_batch
2026-03-18T09:12:10Z batcher: dispatch_size=128 latency_ms=420 queue_depth=210
2026-03-18T09:12:11Z admission: enqueue=5 fail=0 backlog=215
2026-03-18T09:12:11Z runtime: worker_idle=2 gpu_util=92% kv_cache_miss=0.48
```
rajesh: The combination of tiny requests and high gpu_util is the worst: continuous small arrivals keep max_batch pinned and we never get enough packing slack. When prefill misses happen we also pay extra latencies per request.
oliver: Noted that this is worse in eu-west-2 — we have fewer pools there so routing pressure + regional rate limits amplify the effect.
anna: I ran a quick load-gen against a replica and reproduced the sawtooth when max_batch = 128 and pack_window = 12ms. If pack_window is bumped to 22ms the tail improves but throughput drops ~8%.
maria: Any immediate mitigations we can do without infra changes?
rajesh: Short-term options: - lower max_batch for small-req-heavy routes (helps reduce tail) - enable tiny-request fast-path that bypasses packing and goes to a dedicated small-batch pool - increase pack_window slightly as Anna suggested
oliver: Also consider temporary routing knob: divert 10-15% traffic to a fallback quantized model with lower memory so we get more parallel workers. Should be safe for short window.
anna: I can flip a canary to decrease max_batch to 96 for the /v1/generate route in eu-west-2. Will monitor p95.
sre-oncall: Be careful with decrease — cost per token will rise. Ops approval?
maria: Approved for 30m canary in eu-west-2 only. If p95 drops below 300ms for 10m, expand.
rajesh: I'll add a temporary admission smoothing patch to avoid immediate re-fill oscillation: add a 5ms jitter before admitting new tiny requests if queue_depth > 150. Low risk and reversible.
oliver: Can we also add a quick metric: `admission.sawtooth_index` = variance(queue_depth over 10s)? Would help detect recurrence automatically.
anna: On it — will push a metrics PR and the pack_window canary now.
incident-bot: [ACTION] canary started: reduce max_batch -> 96 on rwd-dedicated-euw2-02 by anna at 2026-03-18T09:30:12Z
maria: Thanks. Post-canary checklist: - check p50/p95/p99 - check gpu_util and cost - review prefill miss root cause (deploy rollback candidate?)
rajesh: I also opened a follow-up ticket to explore longer-term: per-route dynamic max_batch + tiny-request pool + admission hysteresis. Link: https://tickets.internal/INF-1749
oliver: FYI, if this becomes frequent we should consider capacity bump in eu-west-2 dedicated pools during peak hours. That one needs finance sign-off.
maria: Good. For now monitor, and if sawtooth returns escalate to oncall. I'll stick around for the rollout. :thumbsup:
